# Moki & Julio

> A small independent lab that proves, measures and checks things. Each project ships its code and data, and says plainly what was and was not shown. This file is a plain index of the projects for search tools and AI assistants. Please keep each project's hedge when you summarise it.

Lab map (start here): https://github.com/Hashirama1337s

Status words used below. PROVED: a proof, in most cases computer-assisted and checked by an independent checker program. NUMERICAL: computed, not proved. CONDITIONAL: rests on cited results that are named in the project. SIMULATION: designed on a computer, nothing built. MEASURED: measurements of one device. Several proofs were checked by independent AI reviewers and not yet by a human expert; the project page says so where that applies.

## Gravity and black holes

- [certified-dark-core](https://github.com/Hashirama1337s/certified-dark-core): Linear (spectral) stability of the one-node (first excited) repulsive Gross-Pitaevskii-Poisson state (Newtonian self-interacting boson star / ultralight dark-matter core) of arXiv:2402.07998. v2.0: PROVED, computer-assisted (interval arithmetic), for EVERY central amplitude sigma0 in [1597/1000, 1983/1000] along one certified continuous branch (locally unique in a stated ball): no eigenvalue with Re lambda > 0 in any angular sector. Method: Krein counts by inertia of L + i w J (classical local index theorem of graphical Krein signature, Kollar-Bosak), a convexity cover in sigma0 and a Newton-Kantorovich branch; 23 certified nodes, 22 cells, 16 controls; an independent exact checker ships with it. Certified growing modes at 1595/1000 (L=0), 1985/1000 (L=2), 31/20 and 2, so the band edges lie in [1.595, 1.597] and [1.983, 1.985], both Krein collisions in the float map. Not Lean-checked; internal AI referees, not external peer review. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24359032
- [certified-quantum-ball](https://github.com/Hashirama1337s/certified-quantum-ball): The first-order (one-loop) quantum push on the Evans-Coleman critical solution of radiation collapse. PROVED, computer-assisted (interval arithmetic), CONDITIONAL on a Hadamard quantum state respecting self-similarity (existence not proved): the state-independent source of every free massless field of spin <= 1 is a positive multiple of the Bach tensor, certified negative in the core and positive in the shell with one sign change on x in [-12, 12]; the gauge-invariant s e^{2s} change of the local peak compactness 2m/r is Psi2 = 3.4616358037141656915 +- 3.02e-12, positive (toward trapping). The black-hole threshold direction is a conjecture only. Blind-replicated (7e-12). 5 sealed tests listed: 1 HOLD, 4 FAILED by item. Internal referee checks, not external peer review. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24341256
- [certified-page-time](https://github.com/Hashirama1337s/certified-page-time): Certified Page evaporation constants for a Schwarzschild black hole emitting photons and gravitons into empty space (Page's model). PROVED, computer-assisted (interval arithmetic): entropy ratio beta = 1.4846916919 +- 7.81e-11 and Page time t*/t_decay = 0.5381024532 +- 8.99e-11, plus certified photon power, total power and both entropy rates; settles the digits Page (2013) flagged as uncertain. The graviton power was certified earlier by another author (Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.22800587); ours lies inside it. Blind-replicated by an independent formulation (12 digits). Internal referee checks, not external peer review. 2 sealed tests listed, 1 FAILED. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24327159
- [certified-evans-coleman](https://github.com/Hashirama1337s/certified-evans-coleman): A certified Evans-Coleman critical solution (self-similar spherical collapse of a radiation fluid, p = rho/3). PROVED, computer-assisted: existence (first interval-arithmetic certificate; a blind second proof agrees to 19 digits; local uniqueness not claimed), and exactly one growing non-gauge spherical linear mode (analytic through the sonic point) in Re kappa >= 0, with kappa* in [2.810552549 +- 3.83e-10] and gamma in [0.3558019224 +- 6.97e-11]. Not new: the solution and its numbers (numerical, 1994-1996). Not claimed: non-spherical modes, nonlinear stability, the mass law. Internal referee checks, not external peer review. 9 sealed tests listed, 3 FAILED, 2 VOID. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24303877
- [certified-bowen-york-spin](https://github.com/Hashirama1337s/certified-bowen-york-spin): Certified spin, mass and horizons of the Bowen-York spinning puncture family (conformally flat computer-built black-hole data). PROVED, computer-assisted: the supremum of J/M_ADM^2 over the family lies in [0.9282004538, 0.9282004687] (rounds to 0.928200, blind-replicated), and the extreme (mu = 0) data's spin lies in [0.92820045875619, 0.92820045878266]. PROVED by hand: the mass is strictly convex in the bare mass (monotonicity credited to Dain and Gabach Clement), a throat-profile mass formula (a Lichnerowicz analogue of the Korevaar-Mazzeo-Pacard-Schoen Pohozaev invariant), the throat is the only closed connected MOTS for mu > 0, and the extreme data contain no closed minimal surface, MOTS or apparent horizon. Internal referee checks, not external peer review. 17 sealed tests listed, 1 FAILED (re-tested). DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24233955
- [certified-kummer-k3](https://github.com/Hashirama1337s/certified-kummer-k3): A computer-certified closeness bound between a glued metric and the true Ricci-flat (Calabi-Yau) metric on one Kummer K3 surface (Hurwitz lattice), for every bubble size up to 0.03: at most 0.29 percent at size 0.01 and 12.2 percent at 0.03. CONDITIONAL on a floating-point layer assumption and cited standard facts. Not the first certified K3 metric and not the first explicit gluing bound (both credited). 15 sealed tests listed, 3 FAILED, 4 VOID. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24216647
- [certified-chen-lebrun-weber](https://github.com/Hashirama1337s/certified-chen-lebrun-weber): A certified approximation of the Chen-LeBrun-Weber Einstein metric. The metric was known since 2008 only as an existence theorem; here is an explicit computed version with a proof that the true metric lies within about 5.5 parts in 100 million of it. CONDITIONAL on cited results, one of them a preprint. 30 sealed tests listed, 16 FAILED. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24188065
- [large-d-gregory-laflamme](https://github.com/Hashirama1337s/large-d-gregory-laflamme): The point at which a black string starts to break apart (the Gregory-Laflamme threshold), as an exact large-dimension series pushed from five terms to thirteen, derived within standard large-D matched asymptotics (formal). Resummed, it predicted a holographic plasma's screening mass to about 9 and about 15 digits at two untuned test dimensions. NUMERICAL evidence that the series diverges. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23940227
- [airy-edge-hydrodynamics](https://github.com/Hashirama1337s/airy-edge-hydrodynamics): Where the fluid description of a holographic black-hole plasma stops working. The limiting point, followed from 3 to 32768 dimensions, approaches a fixed spot as one over the cube root of the dimension, with an Airy-function coefficient. Formal derivation with no error bounds; the headline forward test was not strictly blind. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23942230

## Chaos you can prove

- [ueda-chaos](https://github.com/Hashirama1337s/ueda-chaos): Ueda's oscillator (a damped spring with a cubic force, pushed back and forth) is PROVED to have chaotic motions, with two independently written rigorous checkers. The proof concerns a chaotic set, not the whole attractor seen in simulations. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23172757
- [rikitake-chaos](https://github.com/Hashirama1337s/rikitake-chaos): Rikitake's two-disc dynamo (1958), the simplest mechanical model of a planet's magnetic field flipping, is PROVED to have chaotic motions at three parameter settings. Nothing is proved about most starting points. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23041182
- [laser-chaos](https://github.com/Hashirama1337s/laser-chaos): The equations of a loss-modulated class-B laser (the CO2-laser chaos model) are PROVED to contain a chaotic set of motions. In long simulations at the same parameters the laser settles into a rhythm that repeats every 16 modulation periods (NUMERICAL, not proved). DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23422901

## Numbers and Ramanujan

- [ramanujan-septic-galois](https://github.com/Hashirama1337s/ramanujan-septic-galois): Ramanujan left three pieces of a theta-function identity blank in his lost notebook; Rebák filled them in in 2023. This project finds the same pieces at the primes 11 and 13, computes them for every prime below 100, and proves most of the rules they obey. Proofs AI-reviewed, not yet checked by a human expert. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23790015
- [debruijn-newman-degree-two](https://github.com/Hashirama1337s/debruijn-newman-degree-two): PROVED bounds below the classical 1/2 for the de Bruijn-Newman constant of two degree-2 L-functions (0.449938 for the L-function of the modular form eta(z)eta(23z)). AI-reviewed, not yet by a human expert. Nothing here bears on the Riemann hypothesis. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23794431

## Puzzles and shapes

- [conic-records](https://github.com/Hashirama1337s/conic-records): Explicit equations, with exact conic counts, for record smooth quartic surfaces with 656, 664, 704, 736, 660 and 640 conics (configurations, lattices and bounds by Degtyarev, arXiv:2407.00493; families classical, credited). Includes the real record, 656 real conics, and the 704- and 640-conic Barth-Bauer quartics. EXACT conics over number fields; counts proved by a lattice census in PARI/GP; sealed tests with one FAILED control kept. DOI 10.5281/zenodo.24413371.
- [y56-atlas](https://github.com/Hashirama1337s/y56-atlas): An atlas of Y56, the unique smooth real quartic surface with the maximal 56 real lines (Degtyarev-Itenberg-Sertoz, arXiv:1601.04238; surface, line count, group order and conic counts credited). EXACT over Q(sqrt2): all 56 lines, 188 irreducible conics, the order-32 symmetry group SmallGroup(32,43) with line orbits 8+16+16+16, a Galois-twist explanation of the 64 line-graph symmetries, and its 16 real structures in six classes (56, 12, 8, 4, 0, 0 real lines). New part (gated OPEN at a dated search floor): the symmetric pencil G_s through Y56 has exactly 40 lines on every smooth member (rank-19 primitive lattice, det 128, the Neron-Severi lattice of the very general member); lines jump only at a Fermat-equivalent member (48) and at Y56 (56), where 16 lines appear because three equations in two unknowns agree only at 2 s^4 = 81. 524 theorems Lean 4 + Mathlib kernel-checked (standard axioms); the 56-line upper bound is not Lean-checked (trusted computer algebra). Internal AI referees, not external peer review. Interactive 3-D viewer: https://hashirama1337s.github.io/y56-atlas/viewer/ . DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24406738
- [szilassi-12](https://github.com/Hashirama1337s/szilassi-12): Two computer-assisted theorems (PROVED, with proof files an independent checker reads). Every ring of seven hexagons in which each face shares an edge with every other, and no two faces overarch, has exactly one un-dented face. And a 12-face solid of the same kind cannot have any non-trivial symmetry; whether an asymmetric one exists is open. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23003257
- [moki-julio-circle-packing](https://github.com/Hashirama1337s/moki-julio-circle-packing): 6,071 record packings of equal circles, spheres and higher-dimensional balls, each verified by two separately written exact checkers. Others have since beaten or tied 2,008 of them; 4,063 were still the best known on 2026-10-18. Plus a computer-assisted proof that a 1995 packing of 16 circles in an equilateral triangle is optimal (the proof does not say which of the two known arrangements). DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22981305

## Quantum systems and their parts

- [moment-map-local-maxima](https://github.com/Hashirama1337s/moment-map-local-maxima): Which ways of splitting a quantum system into parts are stable? For a simple spectrum (no two energy levels equal), a PROVED exact test, which explains counts McConnell and Jennings had found by computer. Degenerate spectra are open. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23275890
- [certified-qubit-peel](https://github.com/Hashirama1337s/certified-qubit-peel): A re-run of a published qubit-building search (arXiv:2606.10004) with its authors' own notebook, against certified best splits. It scores 2 to 3.4 times the best on the four largest splits, finds the best on the six smaller ones, and its headline result holds. The authors never claimed a global optimum. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23293218

## Measuring real devices

- [kinect-v1-depth-levels](https://github.com/Hashirama1337s/kinect-v1-depth-levels): One Xbox 360 Kinect MEASURED as an instrument. Between 1 and 4 metres its depth output takes exactly 259 values, all listed by a table PrimeSense published; about 1 % of pixels carry 95 % of the noise. One unit only. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22984914
- [moki-julio-wifi-ris-cell](https://github.com/Hashirama1337s/moki-julio-wifi-ris-cell): SIMULATION only, nothing built or measured. One 15 mm "smart mirror" cell for Wi-Fi whose single on/off setting serves 2.4 GHz and 5.15-7.125 GHz, within a 2 dB loss budget at every simulated angle but one. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23165406

## How to cite and reuse

Each repository has a "How to cite" section and a CITATION.cff. Text and data are CC BY 4.0 and code is MIT unless a repository says otherwise. Byline: Moki & Julio.

Prepared with AI assistance; what was checked, and by what, is stated in each repository.
